cards.hearing: You may hear that interest rates ticked higher again, and mortgage rates crept up with them.
cards.why: Higher interest rates can mean a bigger monthly payment on a new house, a car loan, or a credit card balance, so people notice it when they are borrowing money.
cards.but: But rates moving a little in one week is not the same as a change to your long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture someone shopping for a new car and the sticker price goes up a touch the same week they walk into the lot. Frustrating, sure. It does not mean they cancel the whole plan to get a car someday.
say: We watch rates, we do not chase them.
A small move in rates is weather. Your plan is the season.

cards.hearing: You may hear that oil prices pulled back a bit this week.
cards.why: Oil feeds into what it costs to fill up the car and to ship the stuff that ends up on store shelves, so when it moves, people feel it at the pump.
cards.but: But a dip or a rise in oil for a few days is not something we build a retirement plan around.
cards.story: Picture a gardener checking the forecast every morning and deciding whether to rip out the tomatoes based on one cloudy day. The garden never gets a chance that way. Oil prices are weather. The plan is the soil underneath.
say: Oil can move around. Your plan stays put.
We notice the headline. We do not rebuild around it.
